Issue, creator, and precise bibliographic credits; distinguishes publication date conventions.
Archival original artwork, creator credits, built web-shooters, and the originally narrator-delivered moral.

historical_claims.anchor: In the summer of 1962, a boy who looked like an unlikely superhero appeared in an American comic book.
The story appeared in a publication that was not yet a Spider-Man magazine.
The original drawings now preserved by the Library of Congress let us see a part of this process unusually close to the page itself.
It is customary to name Stan Lee and Steve Ditko as Spider-Man's co-creators,
Jack Kirby contributed earlier design work and the published first-appearance cover also bears his involvement;
historical_claims.source_locator: cover credit; earlier designs discussed in history

historical_claims.anchor: He experiments with his altered strength and movement, and he invents devices for shooting webs.
At a critical moment a fleeing criminal passes near the newly successful performer.
In the 1962 comic, the famous formulation about great power and great responsibility appears in the story's concluding narration, not as a speech Ben gives Peter.
